overview: About 280 teeth, jaws and ankle bones document an early Eocene carnivoraform sample and replace the historical two-tooth picture of “Miacis” latouri.

ecology.diet: Small-prey or insectivorous diet inferred from dentition
ecology.habitat: Warm early Eocene woodland inferred from locality context
ecology.locomotion: Arboreal capability inferred from tarsal anatomy
ecology.bodySize: Small carnivoraform represented by dental and tarsal material
ecology.guild: Small scansorial faunivore inferred from anatomy

evidenceSummary: The catalogued sample supports dental, tarsal and matrix claims but does not demonstrate crown Carnivora, a direct ancestor or the global first carnivoramorphan.

commonNameZh: 西藏化石豹亚科（原始归属）
overview: A partial cranium and associated jaw material entered a combined fossil–molecular analysis; the original Panthera and snow-leopard affinity remain revisable analytical assignments.

ecology.habitat: High-elevation Zanda Basin palaeoenvironment inferred independently
ecology.locomotion: Not preserved by the cranial sample
ecology.bodySize: Pantherine size inferred from partial cranial material
ecology.guild: Large terrestrial carnivore inferred from dentition

traits: Characters used in a combined total-evidence analysis
evidenceSummary: IVPP V18788.1–3 and the original magnetostratigraphic framework are explicit; taxonomic assignment, affinity and Asian biogeographic scenario remain open to revision.

overview: Holotype NUFV 405 preserves about 65% of one skeleton, combining terrestrial limb proportions with traits used to infer freshwater swimming.

ecology.habitat: Freshwater lake setting; habitual habitat inferred
ecology.locomotion: Terrestrial and semiaquatic capability inferred from limb and body proportions

traits: Long tail and freshwater depositional context
evidenceSummary: The associated skeleton supports an anatomical mosaic, while semiaquatic locomotion, pinnipedimorph placement and a freshwater transition are interpretations rather than an ancestor sequence.
